root_cause: Verified. _melee_chase_gate (plan-time COORD-4 attack conversion) decides 'may charge after Advancing' by AIAbilityAnalyzerData.unit_has_ability_containing(unit,'advance') AND (...,'charge'). Every Ork unit carries the Waaagh! army rule whose text contains both words, but the clause applies only while the unit is riled up (War Cry turn + next turn). So outside the Waaagh! the gate always set advance=true, even when a Normal move put the enemy in charge range, and ChargePhase then refuses the charge (no effect_advance_and_charge). Replays: s7468 r3 Stormboyz and s7473 r3 Beast Snagga Boyz both 'advances to attack ... closing to charge range'. Strongest finding s7473, alt (Normal move toward obj_center) 2 seeds: A -1.0 vs B +16.5; B gained Delaying Action kills (destroyed_per_unit +8) and denied the opponent's Punishment secondary (+5 +5 condemned_left) that A conceded after its Advance left it unable to charge. The same text test also exists in _should_unit_advance (AI-GAP-4) and _should_unit_advance_long_trip (RACE-1), where it drives objective-race Advances by Lootas/Boyz in rounds 1-3.
fix_summary: Game-angle, narrow: only the melee chase gate changes. When FIX_WAAAGH_ADVANCE_CHARGE>=0.5 and the text test says advance-and-charge, the gate confirms with EffectPrimitivesData.has_effect_advance_and_charge(unit) - the engine's own test that ChargePhase uses (covers an active Waaagh!, stratagems, detachment/enhancement grants). If the engine says no, the unit is treated as unable to advance and charge: within Normal move + 12" it Normal-moves to attack (keeps the charge), farther away it still Advances to close as before. During an active Waaagh! the flag is set, so Ork melee still Advances+charges. The objective-race Advance paths (AI-GAP-4, RACE-1) are deliberately untouched so round-1/2 racing and secondary-card coverage (units across the table) do not change - the round-2 lesson. Logs [WAAAGH_ADVANCE_CHARGE] when it flips a decision. 0 = base text test exactly.

Normal-move check). test_ai_ability_awareness (touches advance_and_charge text helpers) is 72/1: the failing check is 'unit_has_ability_containing detects fall back in description' in AIAbilityAnalyzer.gd, a file this design does not touch (not caused by this change; not re-run on BASE).

fires: Counted from the replay records (the rollout runner runs --quiet and discards stdout, so the print is not in the kept logs; a fire = an Ork 'moves to attack ... closing to charge range', which base never produces). One fire per game in F0 (P2 Stormboyz), F1 (P1 Beast Snagga) and G0 (P1 Beast Snagga), each at the decision position; 0 fires in the four round-1/3 Lootas/race guardrail games (both players, through the end of the next round). Never fires for non-Ork units without the ability text, nor during an active Waaagh!.
risks: Rounds 1-2: unchanged for objective racing (AI-GAP-4/RACE-1 untouched) and for Ork melee beyond Normal move + 12" (still Advance); the only change is a melee unit already in reach Normal-moves and charges. Rounds 3-5: Ork melee units outside the Waaagh! turn now actually declare charges instead of Advancing into a refused charge - more kills (Delaying Action / Assassination-type destroy secondaries) and stickier objective contests; centre units stay nearer their objective (Centre Ground/hold cards) instead of overrunning. Cost cases: (a) with 9-12" left after the Normal move the charge is unlikely (8-28%), and an Advance would have left the unit ~3.5" closer for next turn / a positional secondary (Behind Enemy Lines, Engage on All Fronts table-quarter reach) - the fix gives up that 3.5" for a long-shot charge; (b) a failed charge ends further back than the base Advance. (c) If the War Cry is saved for a later round, the AI will no longer pre-position with Advances before it. Overall, it acts in fewer than ~1 decision per Ork game in the replays, so full-game drift should be small; verify in the Orks mirror and Custodes vs Orks full-game bench.
